source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Regional Price Parities by State and Metro Area, 2024
methodology: Regional Price Parity (RPP) is BEA's official cost-of-living-difference index across all consumption goods and services, including housing rents. 100 = national average; a state/metro at 110 is about 10% more expensive than average, at 90 is about 10% cheaper. State figures are table SARPP (all 50 states + DC, whole-state blend of metro and non-metro areas). Metro-area figures are table MARPP (384 Metropolitan Statistical Areas; a handful straddle state lines and are listed once per MSA, tagged with every state it touches). BEA does not publish a per-state non-metropolitan breakdown -- only a single national non-metropolitan figure (nationalNonMetroRpp) exists, shown for context, never substituted for a specific state's non-metro area.
verifiedAgainstPrimarySource: 2026-08-06 — every figure compared against BEA's own downloadable regional price parity files (SARPP state, MARPP metro, 2008-2024 vintages): all 51 state parities, all metro parities and the non-metropolitan figure matched exactly, with no state or metro missing. The two rows in BEA's metro file the app does not carry are the national total and the non-metropolitan portion, the latter held here as nationalNonMetroRpp.
